auto_network_tier.description:
The network tier to use when automatically reserving NAT IP addresses.
Must be one of: PREMIUM, STANDARD. If not specified, then the current
project-level default tier is used. Possible values: ["PREMIUM", "STANDARD"]
auto_network_tier.rationale: Determines which Google network tier is used when routing traffic. Premium uses Google's private network which can provide higher speeds and reduced latency, while Standard defaults to using the public internet. Primarily impacts network performance and has no direct impact on security.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Is a precautionary argument preventing the accidental or unauthorised removal of the entire NAT instance. The NAT is a central network gateway that coordinates traffic throughout the network. Deleting it can interrupt critical security protocols that require network connectivity.

drain_nat_ips.description:
A list of URLs of the IP resources to be drained. These IPs must be
valid static external IPs that have been assigned to the NAT.
drain_nat_ips.rationale: A list of inactive IPs that cannot take on new connections. Is used during the transition to new IP addresses and has no direct security impact.

enable_dynamic_port_allocation.description:
Enable Dynamic Port Allocation.
If minPortsPerVm is set, minPortsPerVm must be set to a power of two greater than or equal to 32.
If minPortsPerVm is not set, a minimum of 32 ports will be allocated to a VM from this NAT config.
If maxPortsPerVm is set, maxPortsPerVm must be set to a power of two greater than minPortsPerVm.
If maxPortsPerVm is not set, a maximum of 65536 ports will be allocated to a VM from this NAT config.

Mutually exclusive with enableEndpointIndependentMapping.
enable_dynamic_port_allocation.rationale: Determines how NAT ports are shared within the network. It is used to monitor, log, and trace outbound traffic passing through assigned NAT ports. This argument upholds visibility and accountability by tracking and recording traffic behaviour.

enable_endpoint_independent_mapping.description:
Enable endpoint independent mapping.
For more information see the [official documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/nat/docs/public-nat#specs-rfcs).
enable_endpoint_independent_mapping.rationale: Determines whether an internal IP port uses the same external IP port when routing traffic. This can hinder attacker reconnaissence by making the NATs IP port mapping unpredictable.

endpoint_types.description:
Specifies the endpoint Types supported by the NAT Gateway.
Supported values include:
      'ENDPOINT_TYPE_VM', 'ENDPOINT_TYPE_SWG',
      'ENDPOINT_TYPE_MANAGED_PROXY_LB'.
endpoint_types.rationale: Determines what resource types can use the NAT gateway. Controls gateway routing which can introduce vulnerabilities and an attack surface.

icmp_idle_timeout_sec.description: Timeout (in seconds) for ICMP connections. Defaults to 30s if not set.
icmp_idle_timeout_sec.rationale: Drops inactive ICMP connections after a set amount of time. Can prevent excessively long connections from draining network bandwidth. Primarily boosts network performance with very no direct impact on security.

initial_nat_ips.description:
Self-links of NAT IPs to be used as initial value for creation alongside a RouterNatAddress resource.
Conflicts with natIps and drainNatIps. Only valid if natIpAllocateOption is set to MANUAL_ONLY.
initial_nat_ips.rationale: Sets the public-facing IPs to be used by the NAT. Influences internal resource outbound traffic permissions to third party networks as the NAT IP will be used in the allowlist.

max_ports_per_vm.description:
Maximum number of ports allocated to a VM from this NAT.
This field can only be set when enableDynamicPortAllocation is enabled.
max_ports_per_vm.rationale: Set the maxiumum number of ports that can be allocated to a VM when dynamic allocation is enabled. Affects how many connections a VM can have simultaneously and primarily impacts performance rather than security.

min_ports_per_vm.description: Minimum number of ports allocated to a VM from this NAT. Defaults to 64 for static port allocation and 32 dynamic port allocation if not set.
min_ports_per_vm.rationale: Set the minimum number of ports that can be allocated to a VM when dynamic allocation is enabled. Affects the minimum baseline connections a VM needs to have and primarily impacts performance rather than security.

name.description:
Name of the NAT service. The name must be 1-63 characters long and
comply with RFC1035.
name.rationale: This is the name used to identify the NAT service. Has no security or performance impact and is primarily a reference.

nat_ip_allocate_option.description:
How external IPs should be allocated for this NAT. Valid values are
'AUTO_ONLY' for only allowing NAT IPs allocated by Google Cloud
Platform, or 'MANUAL_ONLY' for only user-allocated NAT IP addresses. Possible values: ["MANUAL_ONLY", "AUTO_ONLY"]
nat_ip_allocate_option.rationale: Sets whether NAT IPs are assigned manually or auto-allocated by Google Cloud. Manually allocating IPs can give greater control over traffic management and permissions than auto-allocation which may unintentionally create trust conflicts.

nat_ips.description:
Self-links of NAT IPs. Only valid if natIpAllocateOption
is set to MANUAL_ONLY.
If this field is used alongside with a count created list of address resources 'google_compute_address.foobar.*.self_link',
the access level resource for the address resource must have a 'lifecycle' block with 'create_before_destroy = true' so
the number of resources can be increased/decreased without triggering the 'resourceInUseByAnotherResource' error.
nat_ips.rationale: A list of IPs used by the NAT for translation. Influences how outbound traffic is viewed and treated by third-party destinations.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Configures the NAT to a specific GCP project. Influences project-level security controls and monitoring.

region.description: Region where the router and NAT reside.
region.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

router.description: The name of the Cloud Router in which this NAT will be configured.
router.rationale: Configures the NAT and its network to a Cloud Router. This configuration influences the capabilities and limitations of a network by the router type chosen.

source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat.description:
How NAT should be configured per Subnetwork.
If 'ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES', all of the
IP ranges in every Subnetwork are allowed to Nat.
If 'ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_PRIMARY_IP_RANGES', all of the primary IP
ranges in every Subnetwork are allowed to Nat.
'LIST_OF_SUBNETWORKS': A list of Subnetworks are allowed to Nat
(specified in the field subnetwork below). Note that if this field
contains ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES or
ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_PRIMARY_IP_RANGES, then there should not be any
other RouterNat section in any Router for this network in this region. Possible values: ["ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES", "ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_PRIMARY_IP_RANGES", "LIST_OF_SUBNETWORKS"]
source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat.rationale: Determines where the NAT is applied in the network. This configures the extent to which internal resources can access the internet.

source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat64.description:
Specify the Nat option for NAT64, which can take one of the following values:
ALL_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS: All of the IP ranges in every Subnetwork are allowed to Nat.
LIST_OF_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS: A list of Subnetworks are allowed to Nat (specified in the field nat64Subnetwork below).
Note that if this field contains NAT64_ALL_V6_SUBNETWORKS no other Router.Nat section in this region can also enable NAT64 for any Subnetworks in this network.
Other Router.Nat sections can still be present to enable NAT44 only. Possible values: ["ALL_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS", "LIST_OF_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS"]
source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat64.rationale: Controls whether all or select IPv6 and NAT64 internal resources can access the internet. This has security impacts on the exposure of internal IPv6 traffic while transmitting through the public internet.

tcp_established_idle_timeout_sec.description:
Timeout (in seconds) for TCP established connections.
Defaults to 1200s if not set.
tcp_established_idle_timeout_sec.rationale: Determines the time in which inactive TCP connections remain established in NAT before they are dropped. This is primarily a performance configuration and has no direct security impacts.

tcp_time_wait_timeout_sec.description:
Timeout (in seconds) for TCP connections that are in TIME_WAIT state.
Defaults to 120s if not set.
tcp_time_wait_timeout_sec.rationale: Determines the time in which TCP connections are retained in the TIME_WAIT state within the NAT. This is primarily a performance configuration and has no direct security impacts.

tcp_transitory_idle_timeout_sec.description:
Timeout (in seconds) for TCP transitory connections.
Defaults to 30s if not set.
tcp_transitory_idle_timeout_sec.rationale: Determines the time before TCP transitory connections in NAT are dropped. Primarily a performance configuration to remove inactive connections.

type.description:
Indicates whether this NAT is used for public or private IP translation.
If unspecified, it defaults to PUBLIC.
If 'PUBLIC' NAT used for public IP translation.
If 'PRIVATE' NAT used for private IP translation. Default value: "PUBLIC" Possible values: ["PUBLIC", "PRIVATE"]
type.rationale: Sets NAT type to public or private IP translation. Determines whether the NAT can share internal resources to the public internet.

udp_idle_timeout_sec.description: Timeout (in seconds) for UDP connections. Defaults to 30s if not set.
udp_idle_timeout_sec.rationale: Drops inactive UDP connections after a set amount of time. Primarily for performance tuning.

log_config.enable.description: Indicates whether or not to export logs.
log_config.enable.rationale: Determines if NAT logs are exported. This is security related in that it closely monitors and records NAT behaviour and activity.

log_config.filter.description: Specifies the desired filtering of logs on this NAT. Possible values: ["ERRORS_ONLY", "TRANSLATIONS_ONLY", "ALL"]
log_config.filter.rationale: Decides the level of detail in NAT logs. This provides greater control over visibility to security teams.

nat64_subnetwork.description:
One or more subnetwork NAT configurations whose traffic should be translated by NAT64 Gateway.
Only used if 'source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat64' is set to 'LIST_OF_IPV6_SUBNETWORKS'

nat64_subnetwork.name.description: Self-link of the subnetwork resource that will use NAT64
nat64_subnetwork.name.rationale: Directly identifies the subnetwork that will use NAT64 translation. Controls which IPv6 resources within a subnet can access the internet which brings about exposure risks.

rules.description: A list of rules associated with this NAT.

rules.description.description: An optional description of this rule.
rules.description.rationale: Plain text documenting the NAT rules. Has no impact on NAT configurations.

rules.match.description:
CEL expression that specifies the match condition that egress traffic from a VM is evaluated against.
If it evaluates to true, the corresponding action is enforced.

The following examples are valid match expressions for public NAT:

"inIpRange(destination.ip, '1.1.0.0/16') || inIpRange(destination.ip, '2.2.0.0/16')"

"destination.ip == '1.1.0.1' || destination.ip == '8.8.8.8'"

The following example is a valid match expression for private NAT:

"nexthop.hub == 'https://networkconnectivity.googleapis.com/v1alpha1/projects/my-project/global/hub/hub-1'"
rules.match.rationale: Defines which rules apply to outbound traffic. Filters and controls the behaviour of outgoing traffic passing through the NAT gateway. Prevents unintended behaviour that may cause vulnerabilities.

rules.rule_number.description:
An integer uniquely identifying a rule in the list.
The rule number must be a positive value between 0 and 65000, and must be unique among rules within a NAT.
rules.rule_number.rationale: Unique identifier for a specific rule to seperate it from others and determines order of application. The ID is a reference point to help avoid unintended changes to rules, while the application order creates a rule priority system which prevents conflicts.

rules.action.description: The action to be enforced for traffic that matches this rule.

rules.action.source_nat_active_ips.description:
A list of URLs of the IP resources used for this NAT rule.
These IP addresses must be valid static external IP addresses assigned to the project.
This field is used for public NAT.
rules.action.source_nat_active_ips.rationale: Which static public IPs will be used by the NAT when creating connections. Is security related in that chosen IPs must be within trusted IP lists to prevent unintended filtering or blocking. Also provides tracability and transparency to traffic from these IPs.

rules.action.source_nat_active_ranges.description:
A list of URLs of the subnetworks used as source ranges for this NAT Rule.
These subnetworks must have purpose set to PRIVATE_NAT.
This field is used for private NAT.
rules.action.source_nat_active_ranges.rationale: Controls which subnetwork source ranges are translated by the NAT and can be accessed through the private NAT. This is a security related argument as it directly configures access controls for the subnetworks and segments the internal network.

rules.action.source_nat_drain_ips.description:
A list of URLs of the IP resources to be drained.
These IPs must be valid static external IPs that have been assigned to the NAT.
These IPs should be used for updating/patching a NAT rule only.
This field is used for public NAT.
rules.action.source_nat_drain_ips.rationale: A list of IPs being made inactive and is used as reference for IP rotations.

rules.action.source_nat_drain_ranges.description:
A list of URLs of subnetworks representing source ranges to be drained.
This is only supported on patch/update, and these subnetworks must have previously been used as active ranges in this NAT Rule.
This field is used for private NAT.
rules.action.source_nat_drain_ranges.rationale: A list of subnetwork range being made inactive and is used as reference for range rotations.

subnetwork.description:
One or more subnetwork NAT configurations. Only used if
'source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat' is set to 'LIST_OF_SUBNETWORKS'

subnetwork.name.rationale: Identifier for the specific subnetwork granted NAT translation. Controls what subnetworks can connect to the internet. Is security related as it exposes internal resources to the public internet.

subnetwork.secondary_ip_range_names.description:
List of the secondary ranges of the subnetwork that are allowed
to use NAT. This can be populated only if
'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES' is one of the values in
sourceIpRangesToNat
subnetwork.secondary_ip_range_names.rationale: Controls whether secondary IP ranges are included in NAT translation. Security related as it determines whether pods and secondary services can connect to the internet and send outbound traffic.

subnetwork.source_ip_ranges_to_nat.description:
List of options for which source IPs in the subnetwork
should have NAT enabled. Supported values include:
'ALL_IP_RANGES', 'LIST_OF_SECONDARY_IP_RANGES',
'PRIMARY_IP_RANGE'.
subnetwork.source_ip_ranges_to_nat.rationale: Sets IP range within a subnetwork to have NAT access. Is security related in that it determines at a subnet level what IPs can connect to the internet and send outbound traffic.
